speaker_role: student/recent admit (Harvard neuroscience student, self-described as admitted to Harvard, Stanford, and MIT)
commercial_incentive: yes - promotes his own website (rishabacademy.com) and a free downloadable guide requiring an email signup, plus his video series and Discord
key_insights: Research was his top extracurricular and, in his account, the main factor behind his admission to Harvard, Stanford, and MIT

Selective summer research programs look for aptitude for research, which can be shown via college-level/AP coursework, strong test scores, or independent STEM projects even without prior research experience
In personal statements, he advises telling a story around accomplishments rather than simply listing awards, which he says is a common mistake in applications he's reviewed
Applicants should tailor essays to each program's specific format (e.g., emphasizing teamwork/communication for programs with a strong residential/social component)
He recommends starting preparation about a year in advance, including planning who to ask for recommendation letters
Interview prep should focus on authentically articulating one's own motivations rather than researching generic 'top interview questions' lists
specific_numbers_or_facts: RSI acceptance rate cited as around 2-3%, attributed to Forbes, per the speaker
notable_or_distinctive: First-person account from an admitted RSI/Harvard student describing his own personal-statement strategy (telling stories about a museum visit and a book rather than listing accomplishments) and a self-made curated list of ~50 research programs.
reliability_notes: Single self-reported success story used partly to promote the creator's own guide/website; advice is plausible but anecdotal and not independently verified, and some claims (e.g., RSI acceptance rate) are attributed to a secondary source (Forbes) rather than verified directly.
